title: Modular GPU Commitment & Surge Governance Playbook
creator: Liam Patel
description: Create a playbook and experiment plan for a modular committed capacity product that separates reservation primitives (GPU-hours, GPU-types, and burst credits) and a governance layer for surge behavior. The goal is to test pricing sensitivity for smaller, composable commitments and a transparent surge governance model that reduces billing churn, improves utilization, and provides clear enterprise SLAs. This ticket covers: product construct design, pricing bands, legal/SQ questionnaire implications, telemetry requirements, experiment hypotheses, and rollout gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: A documented modular product spec that defines three primitives: Reserved Units (hour-based), Shape Anchors (GPU family selection), and Surge Credits (burst pool).
Pricing matrix with at least 3 commitment sizes and 2 surge credit packages and position against existing committed and flex offers.
A/B experiment plan with success metrics and instrumentation requirements for utilization, net revenue retention, and churn impact.
Security/contract questionnaire answers drafted for common enterprise questions: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and isolation guarantees.
Rollout checklist with UI/console mock, billing hooks, legal PS template changes, and a customer pilot cohort identified.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff with Eng, Legal, Solutions. Agreed to pursue a composable commitment model (units + shape anchors + burst credits). Assigned infra telemetry work to ENG-42012.

2025-02-24: Pricing brainstorm with finance produced three anchor points: Small (8 GPU-hrs/day equiv), Medium (32 GPU-hrs/day), Large (128 GPU-hrs/day). Initial uplift recommendations: 12%, 18%, 25% discount vs on-demand for respective commitments.
2025-02-28: Design team shared console flow draft for Purchase + Manage Surge Credits. UX flagged need for clearer language differentiating reserved throughput (SLA-backed) vs best-effort surge.
2025-03-03: Legal requested SQ draft covering: encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS options, audit retention, third-party pen-tests, and incident notification SLAs. Draft prepared and added to links.
decisions: Use hour-based Reserved Units rather than slot-count to simplify metering across shapes.
Surge Credits will be a separate SKU with explicit soft limits and a credit exhaustion policy that gracefully degrades to lower-capacity models rather than hard rejects.
Introduce two SLA tiers mapped to commitments: Silver (99.5% uptime, best-effort burst) and Gold (99.9% uptime, prioritized burst routing and pre-warmed slots).
Run two parallel experiments: price elasticity for Small commitments and usage pattern for Surge Credits.
notes_from_customer_calls: 2025-02-20 call with StreamAI: customers want predictable tail latency guarantees for inference, willing to trade price for guaranteed pre-warm capacity during business hours.

2025-02-26 call with FinDataCo: strong preference for explicit audit log retention and per-tenant KMS keys; asked whether surge credits could be prepaid and isolated per VPC — marked as 'Gold' requirement.
2025-03-01: Pilot candidate identified (HealthML) interested in a Medium commitment plus 2 months of surge credits for a controlled go-live window.
experiment_plan: Experiment A: Price elasticity test for Small commitment. Randomize sign-up flow between Control (current reserved pricing) and Variant (modular Small with surge credits). Track conversion rate, ARR per account, 90-day retention.

Experiment B: Surge credit usage test. Offer 2 surge packages (low and high) to pilot customers. Measure credit consumption, percent of requests served with reserved vs surge capacity, and incident rate.
Instrumentation: add metrics for reserved_utilization, surge_credit_burn_rate, prewarm_hit_rate, overage_incidents, and customer-facing latency_p50/p95/p99.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal beta: enable feature flag for internal accounts and Solutions Eng demos.
Phase 1 - Pilot: onboard 3 enterprise customers (HealthML, FinDataCo, StreamAI) for 8-week pilots. Collect feedback and iterate.
Phase 2 - Gradual public launch: exposed in Console for new signups with a guided purchase flow and pricing transparency microsite.
Gating: legal signoff on SQ answers, engineering telemetry availability, and pilot success metrics met (>=10% uplift in NRR or >=5% reduction in churn risk for pilot cohort).
open_questions: How do we bill unused Reserved Units at the end of monthly commitment? (rollover vs forfeiture vs conversion to credits)
Should Surge Credits expire or roll month-to-month for active commitments?
Do we provide automated model fallbacks when credits are exhausted or require explicit customer opt-in for degradations?
What penalty/credit model do we use if we miss Gold SLA targets? (service credits vs pro-rated refunds)
How granular should Shape Anchors be (broad families vs specific instance types) to avoid metering complexity?
